Subject: Re: Sudden 429s + latency spike in production — urgent

Hi all,

Quick technical summary from the first-pass investigation (logs + control plane traces attached):

What I see:
- At 08:44 PDT a change to global "safety_band" rounding logic was deployed (internal rollout) which tightened the effective burst_window threshold for accounts with per-minute quotas.
- CardioFit's quota configuration: quota=120k tokens/minute, burst_window=30s, safety_band=0.1 (10%). The rounding bug reduced the burst allowance by ~30% for this account class, dropping the effective tokens available in the burst window below the observed QPS peaks.
- Result: token bucket exhaustion then rapid 429s. When the safety guard tripped, we also saw synchronous backpressure that increased tail latency for inflight requests.

Immediate actions taken (10:00 PDT):
- Temporarily lifted safety_band enforcement on CardioFit's routing policy.
- Applied a one-time burst uplift to match historical peak usage (+40% for 1 hour).
- Pushed a flag to stop the problematic rounding change from affecting existing quota windows.

Attachments included: policy-diff.txt (config diff), traffic-samples.jsonl (sample request timestamps).

Next steps I recommend:
1) Keep uplift for the next 60 minutes while we monitor 429 and latency metrics.
2) Full rollback of rounding change from the rollout and a canary of the corrected logic.
3) Automated alert rule to surface sudden drops in effective burst allowance next to quota changes.
4) Postmortem and customer-facing RCA within 48h.

I'll push monitoring dashboards for CardioFit and share a readout in 30 minutes.

-Karthik
Karthik Iyer
Senior SRE, Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: Sudden 429s + latency spike in production — urgent

Hi Sarah —

Thanks for being on the call earlier. Per Karthik's note, we applied a short-term uplift and stopped the rollout that caused the constraint. Early telemetry looks good: 429s are down ~95% and p99 latency is trending back to baseline.

Customer plan and next steps:
- Maintain the temporary burst uplift until 12:15 PDT, then step down to a 10% uplift for 24h while we validate corrected rollout.
- We will run a corrective canary in a staging ring and then schedule a controlled rollout with tighter gating and a pre-deploy test that simulates burst behavior.
- We propose a one-time service credit for the customer for the affected window; looping in Laura for approval and guidance on the credit amount.

We'll share the 24h postmortem and the RCA doc. Please send any additional logs you want included in the RCA.

Best,
Monica Patel
Customer Success Manager, Redwood Inference

Subject: Exec note: CardioFit interruption caused by safety_band rounding change — request for credit approval + postmortem

Laura —

Summary (for exec review):
- Impact: CardioFit (production, us-west-2) experienced a 15–20 minute period of elevated 429s and p99 latency spikes beginning 08:44 PDT due to a rounding bug in the recently deployed safety_band logic that reduced effective burst allowance for per-minute quotas.
- Mitigation: SRE lifted safety enforcement and applied a 40% temporary burst uplift; 429s dropped ~95% within 10 minutes.
- Customer business impact: two customer-facing features experienced degraded availability; CardioFit reported customer complaints and paused a small internal campaign.

Requests:
1) Approve a one-time service credit to CardioFit for the incident window (proposed amount: USD 12,000) and authorize the CS team to expedite the credit.
2) Approve an incident postmortem to be published to the customer within 48 hours and a follow-up engineering action plan:
   - Rollback fix pushed and safe canary validated (Karthik)
   - Add an automated guard that warns on >10% effective reduction in burst allowance for accounts with historical burst patterns
   - Update release checklist to include a synthetic burst test for quota/safety changes

Attachments: mitigation-playbook.pdf (internal runbook excerpt).

Please reply with approval or adjustments. If you prefer, I can present the brief to Execs in the 16:00 sync.

—Stephanie
Stephanie Nguyen
Account Exec, Redwood Inference
